uncertainties.detail: The upstream record supplies an exact name, Turkish context and one current vessel. Public sources confirm Crocus's specifications, Turkish base, refit and charter activity but disclose no owner. No employer, city, relative, middle name, birth date, company vehicle or verified social profile connects the owner record to a public candidate, leaving confidence at 50.

İnmak's official pages and Dun & Bradstreet establish a Turkish industrial-machinery founder and chairman named Atila Köse in Istanbul. This candidate is geographically and economically plausible but remains only a namesake hypothesis because no reviewed source links him, İnmak, Baran Köse or Berk Köse to Crocus. His biography and business are not transferred.

The owner record includes a 50-by-50-pixel portrait, while İnmak publishes a larger but evidently older corporate portrait. Their different ages, resolution and presentation do not support reliable facial identification. No identity claim is based on visual comparison.

A Turkish education-ministry document identifies an Atila Köse as a physics and astronomy teacher, and French business data records another exact Latin-script Atila Kose as a former repair-shop proprietor. Wider search results contain additional Atilla Köse variants. These facts demonstrate collision risk and are excluded from the owner biography.

YachtBuyer matches the upstream 39.3-metre and 213-GT measurements. SuperYacht Times currently reports 42.67 metres with the same 213 GT, likely reflecting a different post-refit length convention. This discrepancy does not affect identity resolution, and neither public source names the owner.

Turkish nationality, Turkey residence and birth country, male gender and Alive status remain upstream facts. No strong public source supports middle names, a birth date, birthplace, secondary nationality, known-for title, LinkedIn, Instagram, personal website or company website for the unresolved owner.

All four wealth fields remain Unknown, and no approved active tag is assigned. Industrial machinery belongs only to the unlinked İnmak candidate; yacht charter activity is not sufficient to classify the owner's wealth. No taxonomy candidate is created.
